replication.target_description: Hypothesis 1: proportion of women listed relative to all persons listed across six occupational categories; one-factor between-subjects ANOVA, main effect of linguistic expression of gender (masculine generics, feminine-masculine word pairs, capital-I, gender asterisk), full final sample.

notes: Original locator p.4 corresponds to journal p.467. Original N=90 is established from the printed 45 female and 45 male participants and the reported full-sample factorial ANOVA; the total is also explicitly printed in the replication paper Table 1 (p.4). Broad page-only locators identify omnibus linguistic-form main effects; these include capital-I (both studies) and gender asterisk (replication), not a single word-pair contrast. Replication uses its primary Hypothesis 1 one-factor ANOVA (.15; N=344); the same page additionally reports a two-factor main effect (.18; N=340), not combined here. Original sensitivity analysis excludes four participants but provides no replacement statistics. The replication narrative calls the findings a replication while also noting a stronger word-pair result than the original (pp.8,10).
